name: OPA partial evaluation -> JPA Specification (row-level filtering)
description: For list endpoints, instead of fetching all rows then filtering in-memory, send the ABAC query to OPA's compile API (partial evaluation) to get back residual conditions, then translate those conditions into a JPA Criteria Specification (or QueryDSL predicate) applied at the database. This pushes authorization into the SQL WHERE clause — correct and efficient. This is the library's differentiating feature; the one comparable OSS project (opa-data-filter) is unmaintained.

name: Batch action evaluation for list endpoints
description: When checking many resources' actions at once (e.g. which actions a user may take on each item in a page), batch them into a single OPA evaluation with adaptive chunking rather than one call per item. Large measured speedups for list endpoints versus per-item calls. Keep a sane chunk size and make it configurable.

OPA response-wrapper DTOs that omit @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) break deserialization the moment OPA decision logging is enabled, because every response then carries an extra 'decision_id' field. The client throws 'Unrecognized field decision_id' and (if it falls back to deny-all) silently denies everything.
resolution: Put @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) on EVERY OPA response wrapper class (and nested decision classes), not just some. Add a test that deserializes a response containing an unknown field.

name: Distinguish error-DENY_ALL from policy-DENY_ALL in partial-eval residuals
description: A failed Compile call (transport/non-200/unparseable) and a policy-unsatisfiable answer both collapse to DENY_ALL, but they must compose differently: a POLICY deny may legitimately be OR-widened (e.g. a hierarchy subtreeSpec alongside an unsatisfiable tag branch), while an ERROR deny means there is no policy answer at all — nothing may widen, no batch fallback may run, the whole list fails closed. Implemented as PartialResult.fromError + PartialResult.error(); AbacQueryService returns List.of() before any composition when fromError. General rule: any Java-side predicate that mirrors a policy clause (SubtreeSpecResolver mirrors inherited_grant) must never outlive the policy engine it mirrors — gate it on 'we actually heard from OPA'.
